newsitem.title: SPAIN: SPANISH BONDS FIRM, LOOKING ABROAD FOR GUIDANCE.
newsitem.headline: SPANISH BONDS FIRM, LOOKING ABROAD FOR GUIDANCE.

text.p: Spanish government bonds edged higher on Monday, following other European markets in what is expected to be quiet trade as the dollar pulled back from recent highs, dealers said.
"The market sees the dollar in the 1.85 per mark zone, and that is calming it down," an analyst said.
No Spanish economic data are due until Wednesday when July consumer prices will be released. July CPI is seen at 1.6 percent, unchanged from June.
An official interest rate cut is not seen until the government formally presents its 1998 budget to Parliament.
